name: CNN / Siamese well-log depth matching family: 1D-CNN vs cross-correlation (Petrophysics 2022); late-fusion multimodal 1D-CNNs (Geophysical Prospecting 2022/2024); Siamese NN depth alignment (SPWLA 2025); Deep Q-learning multi-well depth matching (Petrophysics 2021); SPWLA PDDA 2023 depth-shifting contest; plus Deep Hierarchical Graph Correlation (triplet 1D-CNN embeddings + DP, JMSE 2026) and ROGII 3rd-place Adaptive 1D SDF as in-domain learned correlation

code_availability: PDDA 2023 contest: public data (9 aligned training wells) and top-team solutions in the repo's Solutions folder (notebooks, MATLAB, packages). The Torres Caceres, Siamese and Deep-Q papers have no public code as far as found [uncertain]. DHGC code status unknown [uncertain]. ROGII 3rd place released code with its writeup (not inspected here).
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed journals (Petrophysics 2021/2022, Geophysical Prospecting, JMSE); the SPWLA 2025 conference paper is known from its abstract only; a public competition with leaderboard (PDDA 2023); a Kaggle writeup (ROGII 3rd). Full texts were mostly paywalled or 403; details come from abstracts and search snippets.
extreme_summary: This literature replaces hand-made similarity (cross-correlation, sample-wise differences) with learned similarity. The forms are: 1D-CNNs that regress a bulk shift between two log windows, late-fused across log types; Siamese or triplet 1D-CNN embeddings whose window-to-window similarity feeds DTW or DP; and RL agents that pick shifts. The consistent lesson, including the PDDA contest where all top 5 teams used ML + DTW, is learned local cost + global DP alignment. Its target, though, is small shifts between logs of the same or a nearby well, not 400-level repeated-band ambiguity.
task_definition: Depth matching / alignment: estimate the depth shift (bulk or depth-varying) that aligns a log to a reference log, e.g. LWD vs wireline in the same well (Torres Caceres; Siamese: GR from different logging runs in one well), multiple logs to a reference GR (PDDA contest: shift RHOB, NPHI, RD to GR), or multi-well correlation (Deep Q, DHGC). This is closely analogous to our per-MD-column choice of typewell TVT level, but the shifts are small and the mapping is monotone.
inputs: Pairs of 1D log windows. Torres Caceres: seven log types (GR, resistivity, P/S sonic, density, neutron, PEF) from 6 Ivar Aasen wells (Norwegian North Sea). Siamese: GR vs GR. PDDA: reference GR + misaligned RHOB/NPHI/RD from 9+3 wells. DHGC: GR windows from 8 North Sea wells. ROGII 3rd SDF: lateral GR + trajectory (4-block TCN) and typewell GR/TVT context (3-block TCN).
target_parameterisation: Bulk shift scalar (1D-CNN per log type; late fusion aggregates shifts); a warping path over a learned cost matrix (Siamese/DHGC + DP); discrete shift actions (Deep Q); corrected log values + per-sample shift (PDDA). ROGII SDF: classification over 256 typewell TVT candidates per lateral row, with the expected TVT as output.
output_representation: Point shift estimate or a single warping path. ROGII SDF gives a per-row softmax over TVT candidates, i.e. the same per-column distribution representation as ours.
architecture: (a) Torres Caceres 2022: supervised 1D-CNN per log type taking reference + shifted windows and estimating a bulk depth shift. Hyperparameters were tuned with three search algorithms; seven models, one per log type. (b) Late fusion 2022/2024: combine the seven CNN shift estimates by averaging, weighted averaging, linear or nonlinear learners, or model-level fusion. (c) Siamese SPWLA 2025: twin networks with shared weights embed reference and unsynchronised GR windows; similarity drives alignment and is claimed to handle irregular (non-bulk) errors without labels (exact encoder, loss and search not in the abstract [uncertain]). (d) Deep Q 2021: DQN with 1D-conv feature extractor; the agent's actions shift logs to maximise a match reward, applied to multiple wells. (e) DHGC 2026: stage 1, a 1D-CNN trained on 177,026 GR-window triplets with triplet-margin loss; stage 2, a feedforward scorer on embedded window pairs builds a cost matrix and DP finds the nonlinear warping path. (f) PDDA 2023 top 5: 1st MDWD + GRU + DTW; 2nd random forest + DTW; 3rd pick-pair-based DTW; 4th ridge + DTW; 5th CNN + DTW. (g) ROGII 3rd Adaptive 1D SDF: TCN encoders, a query-key cosine correlation volume (embedding dim 128) over 256 TVT candidates, fused with trajectory progress, formation rate and graph-edge features, GR bias/scale estimated from the known prefix, and a softmax (T=1.75) with expectation output.
core_mechanism: Learn a similarity metric over windows (receptive field of tens of samples) that is invariant to tool-dependent scale, bias, noise and small stretch, and discriminates geologically distinct windows that look alike sample by sample. Metric learning (Siamese/triplet/contrastive, Rank-N-Contrast in ROGII SDF) makes the similarity reflect correspondence distance rather than raw amplitude difference. A global DP/DTW then enforces path consistency. The Siamese abstract explicitly claims robustness where cross-correlation fails on repetitive lithologies (unverified beyond the abstract).
training_objective: Regression of bulk shift (MSE/MAE, Torres Caceres); triplet margin loss (DHGC); Siamese similarity loss (type not stated [uncertain]); DQN temporal-difference loss on a match reward (Deep Q); ROGII SDF: L = CE over the nearest TVT candidate + 0.25 SmoothL1(TVT/10) + 0.10 L_delta + 0.05 Rank-N-Contrast (the RNC loss orders embeddings by TVT distance).
decoding: Argmin or regressed shift; DP/DTW optimal path over the learned cost matrix; greedy policy rollout (DQN); ROGII SDF expectation over the candidate softmax.
metric_consistent_decode: Mostly mode-seeking (DTW/DP single path, argmin shift). ROGII SDF expectation is RMSE-consistent. For us the embedding would be an input channel, not a decode, so this concern moves to our unchanged expectation decode.
evidence_scope: Local windows scored pairwise plus global path via DP/DTW (whole log). ROGII SDF: whole packed lateral sequence vs typewell context.
prefix_conditioning: None in the depth-matching papers. ROGII SDF estimates well-specific GR bias and scale from the known prefix, an explicit in-domain use of heel labels for the similarity function.
propose_vs_select: Mostly single output. In the ROGII use the learned correlation model was a weak standalone candidate (not the strongest) kept for diversity in a softmax gate. For us the natural slot is as an extra input channel (a learned cost slice) rather than as a candidate.
physical_constraints: Monotone depth warping (DTW/DP), bounded shifts; bulk-shift assumption in the Torres Caceres CNN. None of these methods handle non-monotone laterals that go up and down through strata; ROGII SDF handles this by per-row classification without monotonicity.
dataset: Torres Caceres: 6 wells, Ivar Aasen field (4 train/select, 2 inference); late fusion: semi-synthetic data from 3 North Sea wells, tested on 2 real wells. Siamese: GR logs from different logging methods in one well [uncertain]. PDDA 2023: 9 aligned wells for training/validation and 3 misaligned test wells from one field. DHGC: 8 Norwegian North Sea wells, 177,026 triplets. ROGII: Kaggle training wells + synthetic.
synthetic_to_real: Semi-synthetic shifting of real aligned logs is the standard: apply known shifts to aligned logs to create labels (late fusion; PDDA training wells are aligned, so shifts can be simulated). Siamese is claimed label-free (self-supervised pairs). No real-to-real domain gap handling reported beyond normalisation.
metric_and_performance: 1D-CNN vs CC: mean Pearson correlation after CNN matching differs from CC by only 10^-1 to 10^-2, so the CNN is competitive but not superior; it does better on some log types (resistivity). Siamese SPWLA 2025: Pearson correlation 0.003 to 0.878 after alignment, Euclidean distance reduced by 74.6%, beats CC in nonlinear scenarios, slower than CC (abstract only). PDDA 2023: scores are rank-averaged NMSE of corrected logs and MAD of shifts; top 5 within 550-564 points, all DTW-based hybrids. DHGC: claims speedups over DTW with retained accuracy (no numbers retrieved [uncertain]). ROGII 3rd SDF: standalone RMSE weaker than the HMM/PF/NN candidates (exact number not in the local excerpt), but locally selected by the gate.
comparability: Very low for the depth-matching papers: different task (small monotone shifts, same or nearby well), different metrics (Pearson, NMSE, MAD), tiny well counts. ROGII 3rd SDF is directly comparable in task and data: a learned-embedding correlation volume gave a weaker standalone model than the physics/tracker candidates, and its value was diversity.
validation_protocol: Well-level holdout (2 inference wells in Torres Caceres; 3 hidden test wells in PDDA), which is fold-safe at the well level but tiny. Siamese: single-well demonstration. ROGII 3rd: GroupKFold OOF, with a known CV 5.29 vs private 5.84 gap for the full gated system.
inference_budget: Cheap. A 1D-CNN or TCN embedding of 345 lateral windows and 400 typewell windows plus a 345x400 cosine volume costs milliseconds on GPU and under a second on CPU. The Siamese paper notes it is slower than CC, which is irrelevant at our scale.
repeated_layers: This is the stated motivation (the Siamese abstract says cross-correlation gives false matches on repetitive lithologies). But a window embedding can only separate repeated bands whose windows differ somewhere inside the receptive field. Truly self-similar bands stay ambiguous under any local similarity, which is why every method pairs it with a global DP. In our setting the U-Net already aggregates local evidence over a large receptive field, so the marginal gain on band confusion depends on whether a pretrained metric captures invariances (GR bias/scale per well, stretch from relative dip) that the U-Net fails to learn from the raw |GR_lat - GR_tw| slice.
drift: Not addressed directly. Invariance to GR scale and bias in a learned embedding could reduce drift caused by GR calibration mismatch, which ROGII SDF handles explicitly by estimating bias and scale from the prefix. Geometric drift (slow dip error) is outside the scope of similarity learning.
uncertainty_and_calibration: None of the depth-matching papers report calibrated uncertainty. ROGII SDF uses a fixed temperature 1.75 softmax, which is a crude calibration.
where_to_use: As extra channels in the 16-channel cost image built in experiments/arch/seq_NN_dataset.py: a learned cosine-similarity slice between embedded lateral windows (along MD) and embedded typewell windows (along TVT), next to or replacing gr_abs_diff (+-0.25 ft shifted variants) and gr_signed_diff. Alternatively, as a learnable feature-extractor stage inside the model (stereo-style learned correlation volume, see B01) computed end-to-end with the U-Net.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (about 51%), specifically cases where amplitude-level differences look alike but window shape differs. Secondarily, drift induced by GR calibration mismatch between lateral and typewell.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Today the cost image uses sample-wise hand-made interactions: _make_gr_abs_diff_channel computes |(GR_lat[i] - GR_tw[j]) / std| for every MD column i and TVT level j (plus +-0.25 ft shifted typewell variants, signed diff, ratio/compression residuals, |TVT_tw - visible TVT|, PF and XY-neighbour channels). Window-level similarity is learned only implicitly by the ConvNeXt/FastViT encoder from these slices, trained on our small real set plus 85% synthetic. What we do not have: (a) a similarity metric pretrained with a metric-learning objective (triplet, InfoNCE, Rank-N-Contrast) that explicitly contrasts the true TVT level against hard repeated-band negatives; (b) invariance to per-well GR gain and bias learned by design (we use a global diff_std normaliser; the ROGII 3rd SDF estimated per-well bias and scale from the prefix); (c) stretch/compression invariance, since a lateral MD window maps to a typewell TVT interval whose length depends on relative dip, which a 1D embedding trained with stretch augmentation handles and a pointwise difference cannot; (d) learnable, not fixed, feature channels, which is the core stereo lesson (GC-Net/PSMNet correlate learned features, not raw pixels). What we already do: the U-Net is effectively the learned aggregator plus global reasoning, which plays the DP role these papers bolt on, so any gain must come from the feature/metric side only.
proposed_experiment: E1 (pretrain the embedding, fold-safe): new module experiments/arch/seq_NN_log_embed.py. Two 1D TCN/CNN encoders (or one shared, Siamese) over GR windows of W in {32, 64} samples at our downsampled MD and TVT resolution, 32-64-dim L2-normalised output. For each training lateral column i with known TVT t_i, the positive is the typewell window centred at t_i and the negatives are all other 399 TVT levels. Use InfoNCE over the column, which is a per-column softmax, plus a Rank-N-Contrast or distance-weighted soft target so near levels are not penalised like far bands. Mine hard negatives from the top-k gr_abs_diff minima at repeated bands. Augment with random per-well GR gain/bias, noise and lateral stretch in [0.5, 2] to emulate relative dip. Train only on training-fold wells (same split as the U-Net) plus synthetic. Report the embedding-alone expectation RMSE on holdout as a diagnostic. E2 (channel ablation): add channel names 'gr_emb_cos' (and optionally 'gr_emb_cos_w32', 'gr_emb_cos_w64') to seq_NN_dataset.py next to gr_abs_diff, computing the cosine volume from the frozen encoder at data-prep time and caching it. Config in seq_NN_cfg.py. Arms: (A) control = current 16 channels; (B) +gr_emb_cos; (C) gr_emb_cos replacing gr_abs_diff and its shifted variants. ConvNeXt-small, 150 epochs, 2 seeds each, evaluated with seq_NN_holdout_eval.py on the 155 holdout wells and seq_NN_robust_compare.py (noise floor +-0.39 ft). Break down the delta by error anatomy (wrong_mode / blend / drift) with posterior_analysis.py. E3 (only if B beats A): an end-to-end version where the encoder is trainable inside seq_NN_models.py (correlation-volume layer before the U-Net stem, initialised from E1), then distil into FastViT as usual.
implementation_effort: Medium. The encoder and InfoNCE training are about 300 lines; the channel plumbing in seq_NN_dataset.py already has a pattern for new cost channels; caching the volumes avoids retraining cost per epoch. The end-to-end E3 is medium-high because of memory for a 345x400xD volume.
gpu_cost: E1: small, well under an hour on the RTX 5060 8 GB (tiny 1D encoders, 345x400 logits per lateral). E2: the same as baseline training per arm (3 arms x 2 seeds = 6 baseline-scale runs), with one extra input channel. E3: a D=32 correlation volume at 345x400 is about 4.4 M floats per sample, which fits in 8 GB at modest batch size.
distillation_compatibility: Fully compatible: the embedding channel is an input feature, computed identically for teacher and student, so KD on output posteriors is unchanged. For E3, the student can share the frozen encoder.
error_correlation_with_ours: Low diversity if used as a channel (same model, same decode); its purpose is to improve the single model, not to be a blend member. As a standalone candidate (embedding-only expectation), ROGII 3rd shows such a model is weak but decorrelated. Our prior learned-gate failures argue against using it as a gated candidate.
risk: (1) The U-Net may already learn equivalent window features from gr_abs_diff; the 1D-CNN vs CC paper found CNN only on par with plain cross-correlation, and ROGII 3rd's learned-correlation model was the weakest candidate. (2) Pretraining data is the same limited set (15% real), so the metric can overfit to training typewells; fold leakage is a risk if the encoder sees holdout wells. (3) Local similarity cannot resolve genuinely self-similar bands, and the band-confusion share needs more evidence, which an embedding of the same GR does not add. (4) Depth-matching results transfer poorly: small monotone shifts within the same well are a different regime from choosing among 400 TVT levels on a non-monotone lateral. (5) Negative results at 60 epochs for other architecture changes (axial attention, RAFT) show that input or architecture tweaks are often within the +-0.39 ft noise floor, so a multi-seed comparison is needed.
notes: The strongest in-domain evidence is not the depth-matching papers but ROGII 3rd place's Adaptive 1D SDF (TCN encoders + cosine correlation volume + Rank-N-Contrast + prefix-estimated GR bias/scale), which confirms that the idea runs on this exact data and is diverse but weak alone. The PDDA 2023 result (all top-5 are DTW hybrids) and DHGC (triplet embeddings + DP) confirm the 'learned local cost + global alignment' template, which in our pipeline corresponds to 'learned cost channel + U-Net'. Siamese SPWLA 2025 authorship (Acharya, Fabian, Yazidi, Westeng) overlaps with the NTNU/OsloMet BRU21 group behind Torres Caceres. Related items: B01 (stereo learned features and correlation volumes), A11 (pretrained well-log foundation encoders as an alternative source of embeddings), A03 (DTW baseline). Another potentially relevant paper not read: 'Attention-driven convolutional neural network for automated well log depth alignment' (2026, ScienceDirect S2590123026009382).
